:::{#def-new-observation}
#### New observation

A **new observation** is an [input](#def-input) and [outcome](#def-outcome) pair $(\Predvar, \Outvar)$ with the same [joint distribution](random-variables.qmd#def-joint-distribution) as the observations used to choose the prediction,
[statistically independent](independence.qmd#def-indpt) of them,
whose input is observed and whose outcome is not yet observed.

:::

{{< slidebreak >}}

:::{#exm-new-observation}
#### A new observation in the best-predictor exercise

In @exr-best-predictor, suppose the new observation $(\Predvar, \Outvar)$ satisfies the suppositions of its [definition](#def-new-observation),
with the joint distribution given in the exercise as the population it is drawn from.
Suppose also that its input is observed to be $\Predvar = 1$.
Then its unobserved outcome is $4$ or $6$ with equal probability,
and a [prediction](#def-prediction) of $5$ is a guess for that outcome.

:::
